walkthroughs.body_html:
speed = distance ÷ time

A train covers 1500 m in 60 s. Speed = 1500 ÷ 60 = 25 m/s. 🚆

Rearrange to find distance: s = v × t. Or time: t = s ÷ v.

a = (final velocity − initial velocity) ÷ time

A car speeds up from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 4 s. Acceleration = (25 − 5) ÷ 4 = 5 m/s².

If it's slowing down, acceleration is negative.

On a distance-time graph, the gradient is the speed. A steeper line = faster.

On a velocity-time graph, the gradient is acceleration. The area under the line is the distance travelled.

A flat line on a v-t graph means constant velocity — not stopped!

If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.
Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
